Subject: Initial DPA + redlines (training carve-out clarification)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft. Attached are a set of redlines from our privacy team (see StrataCorp_DPA_Redlines.pdf). Two points we need to be explicit about before we can sign:

1) "No training" carve-out: our legal is asking for an explicit prohibition on using customer-provided content to train models or improve model weights, with a limited exception for aggregated telemetry that cannot be re-associated to a customer.
2) Cross-border transfers: we need confirmation of the transfer mechanism for EU data (SCCs or equivalent) and whether any subprocessors outside the US will access content.

Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether the DPA language can be amended to include the proposed carve-out? Also please indicate the signing path (DocuSign/AdobeSign) and expected timeline.

Appreciate it — we are on a tight timeline for procurement.

Best,
Marcy

- We use SCCs for EU transfers and maintain a subprocessor roster; any subprocessor with access to content is listed and requires contractual obligations.

Subject: Re: Initial DPA + redlines (training carve-out clarification)

Hi all,

Per Dylan's note, I've drafted a tight redline for the training carve-out and a short technical note on telemetry. Proposed insert for the DPA, section X (Data Use for Model Development):

"Customer Data shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve the Provider's machine learning models or model weights. Provider may process aggregated, de-identified service telemetry (e.g., system metrics, aggregate latency/usage summaries) for product reliability and operational improvements provided that such telemetry cannot be reconstructed to identify or re-associate with Customer or Customer Data. 

Provider will not retain raw Customer Data for the purpose of model development. Any derivative outputs that incorporate Customer Data will be treated as Customer Confidential Information and not used to improve Provider model families."

A few clarifying bullets:
- We should explicitly exclude "synthetic" or derived datasets that contain verbatim customer content.
- Telemetry carve-out must be limited to non-model uses (ops/infra), and we should add a definition for "de-identified" (e.g., irreversible aggregation + removal of identifiers).
- For transfers: Redwood will use SCCs for EEA transfers and will provide the latest subprocessor list 10 days prior to signature.

If that language is acceptable to StrataCorp, we can incorporate the redline and send for signature. I recommend DocuSign with an audit trail and a deadline for countersignature (10 business days).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
Legal redlines attached in-line to the PDF.

Laura — thanks for the quick and precise language. A few notes from our privacy team after review:

- The proposed clause is close to what we need. Two small requests:
  1) Can you add a sentence that explicitly prohibits use of Customer Data to generate training datasets (not just model weights)? Our vendor policy calls this out specifically.
  2) Can you commit to notifying us of any new subprocessor additions 30 days before they are put into production with access to Customer Data (not just prior to signature)?

- Telemetry: we accept the operational telemetry carve-out provided we get examples of the types of metrics collected and an assurance they are retained no longer than 90 days.

If those two points are acceptable, we are prepared to sign via DocuSign. I'll provide a list of our internal signees (Tom from Security and our GC) later today.

Thanks — aiming to close by end of week.

Best,
Marcy

Marcy — great, we can accept both asks with minor tweaks:

1) Add explicit line to cover generation of training datasets (we'll include the wording below).
2) Subprocessor notice: we can commit to 30 days' notice before a subprocessor with access to Content goes live.
3) Telemetry retention: we'll provide a list of example metrics and commit to 90 days max retention for operational telemetry used for reliability.

Proposed final sentence to insert: "Provider shall not use Customer Data to compile datasets for model training or to generate derivative datasets used for model development; any exceptions must be agreed in writing by Customer."

I'll route the updated DPA through DocuSign once you confirm approvers. Expected DocuSign envelope will include: (1) DPA (redlined + clean), (2) Subprocessor roster snapshot, (3) SCCs reference.
